_doc: The launch controls of `collect.sh negative core` (plan section 8, F), one body each, as data.
The kit renders every body from this file with jq, and TestAssessKitControlsMatchTheRoute
(internal/intelligence/dashboard) renders the same bodies and posts them to the real launch
handler, so a renamed member, a new required member or a changed rule order fails a Go test
A body is `base` with every `@name` filled from the plan answer, then `set` laid over it.
The values: @project_root_hash is the fixture project's hash from /api/security/status,
@run_id the plan's run id, @tool an agent from the plan's allowed_tools, @target the confirmed
loopback target, and @tripwire_digest the plan's prompt digest with its first character
changed. The tripwire is what makes a control unable to start a terminal: the digest is
checked after every eligibility rule and before anything is claimed or started, so a launch
that gets past the rule under test is stopped there with 409 plan_changed. A control row that
answers plan_changed therefore means the body was ACCEPTED (BASE says the body is otherwise
good; any other row answering it means its rule did not fire).
A row with `needs` is built only when that environment variable is set (the kit fills
@needs from it) and is not run by the Go test.

controls.label: BASE the unmodified body is accepted (only the tripwire digest stops it)
E6 sandbox false is not read: the route sandboxes, so the body is accepted as a sandboxed launch
E6 sandbox false is answered by the sandbox rules (a backend that is not grounded: E9, never E6)
E8b an agent that is not proxy routed (NEG_UNROUTED_TOOL)
controls.skip_hint: a launchable agent the Adapters page shows as not proxy routed
